en.title: Wrong Price and Misleading Advertising: What Can You Do?
en.directAnswer: Save the advertisement before it changes. Compare the advertised claim with the price, product, service or conditions actually offered. Ask the seller to explain the difference. Consumer law may apply to misleading acts, but not every typo or misunderstanding creates the same legal remedy.

atAGlance.whoFor: A consumer sees a false price, hidden condition or misleading product claim.
atAGlance.mainRule: Save the advertisement before it changes. Compare the advertised claim with the price, product, service or conditions ac
atAGlance.updateStatus: Use careful wording. The article should not decide that an advertisement is unlawful without the full facts.

en.lawMeaning:
Evidence should show the exact advertisement and what the seller actually charged or provided.

This page gives a general route. A person’s exact rights can change because of facts, documents, deadlines, legal status, court orders or later amendments.
steps: Screenshot the full ad and date.
Use DNCRP where the facts fit consumer law.
evidence: Relevant official notices, receipts, and correspondence
en.simpleExample: A store advertises a price but adds a hidden mandatory charge only at payment. The buyer should save both screens and the final receipt.
commonMistakes: Cropping screenshots so context is lost.
assuming every promotion applies to every customer.
confusing tax/delivery charges with deception without reading terms..
en.specialistTrigger: Large financial loss; medical/safety claim; repeated deceptive scheme; sector-regulated product.
